title: An In Vitro Organ Culture Model of the Murine Intervertebral Disc
protocol: Euthanize animals with CO2 overdose at a flow rate of 2.5-3 L/min for 5 min followed by an additional 2 min of dwelling time.
Disinfect the outside region of the animal by bathing it in a 70% ethanol bath for 2 min before dissection.
Make a longitudinal vertical cut on the dorsal surface of the mouse using small dissection scissors to expose the body cavity.
Make two longitudinal vertical cuts on either side of the animal's spine starting from the first lumbar vertebrae (L1) to the caudal vertebrae (C8).
Carefully remove the spine from L1-C8 from the animal's body cavity using a scalpel, fine forceps, and fine dissection scissors.
Remove excess soft tissues surrounding the spinal column while ensuring not to scrape or injure the IVD on the ventral side.
Dissect the spinal column into vertebrae-disc-vertebrae functional spinal units (FSUs) at the L1/L2, L3/L4, L5/L6, C3/C4, C5/C6, and C7/C8 discs.
Rinse the FSUs in Hank's balanced salt solution supplemented with 1% penicillin-streptomycin for 2 min.
Randomly assign the FSUs into three groups: uncultured and untreated FSUs (Fresh), cultured but untreated FSUs (Control), and cultured and stab treated FSUs (Stab).
Snap freeze the Fresh FSU samples with liquid nitrogen immediately after dissection and store in a -20 °C freezer.
Prepare 500 mL of sterile culture media of 1:1 Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium: Nutrient Mixture F-12 (DMEM:F12) supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Pipette 2 mL of culture media into each well of a 24-well culture plate using 10 mL serological pipettes.
Place each FSU into an individual well in the media-filled 24-well plate following dissection and rinse.
Incubate the samples in a sterile incubator that maintains 37 °C, 5% CO2, 20% O2, and > 90% humidity.
Mechanically injure the Stab group samples via needle puncture of the annulus fibrosus using a sterile 27-gauge needle after an initial culture period of 24 h.
Change media every 48 h by preparing a new media-filled 24-well culture plate and transferring samples from the old plate to the new using sterile tweezers.
Aspirate the old media and dispose of the old culture plate in a biohazard waste bin.
Incubate all samples in media containing 0.75 mg/mL nitro blue tetrazolium chloride for 24 h on the final day of culture.
Freeze all FSUs with liquid nitrogen and store at -20°C until ready for use.
Image FSUs from NF-κβ-luciferase animals at 1, 5, 13, and 19 days to assess NF-κB expression.
Add 10 μL of 1 mg/mL luciferin solution to each well.
Incubate the wells in a sterile incubator at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Image samples for bioluminescence using an imaging system with a 1-minute exposure time and bin setting of 2.
Take a photograph concurrently with the machine and overlay it with the bioluminescence image to determine anatomical location.
Remove bony vertebral bodies from FSU while keeping cartilaginous endplates intact, using a dissection microscope, scalpel, and tweezers.
Attach isolated IVDs to a 1 cm x 1 cm x 0.2 cm aluminum plate using cyanoacrylate glue.
Measure the disc height and width by taking an average of three measurements on the longitudinal axis of each disc using a laser micrometer.
Calculate the disc height ratio by dividing the average disc height by the maximum disc width.
Use measured disc height to calculate input strain values for mechanical testing.
Place the samples in a phosphate buffered saline bath under the compression machine.
Preload the disc to 0.02 N.
Cyclically compress the disc using a sinusoidal waveform at 1 Hz for 20 cycles at the 1% strain level.
Repeat cyclic compression at the 5% strain level for 3 trials each.
Record the load and displacement values of the IVD during compression.
Allow 10 min of resting time between trials to prevent injury.
Calculate the average stiffness from the loading phase of the last cycle.
Calculate the loss tangent from the phase angle between load and displacement data.
Measure the disc wet weight by placing the isolated IVD in a pre-tared centrifuge tube.
Digest the isolated IVDs in 250 µL papain digestion solution overnight at 65 °C.
Centrifuge samples for 10 min at 2,000 x g and collect the supernatant fluid.
Measure the proteoglycan content of the IVD using the dimethylmethylene blue (DMMB) assay with chondroitin sulfate standards.
Prepare DMMB solution according to the recipe provided.
Pipette 30 µL of standards and samples in triplicate in a 96-well plate.
Add 250 µL of DMMB solution to each well.
Read the absorbance of the plate at 525 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Fix samples in 4% paraformaldehyde for 24 h.
Decalcify fixed samples in 5% formic acid for 48 h.
Dehydrate decalcified samples with ethanol.
Embed dehydrated samples in paraffin.
Section embedded samples sagittally at 10 µm thickness using a microtome and apply sections to glass slides.
Stain the sections using Safranin-O/Fast Green.
Stain the sections using DAPI.
Image stained slides at 10X magnification using a light microscope.
Add 300 μL of 350 mg/mL iodine Ioversol solution to the culture media for a final concentration of approximately 50 mg/mL and incubate in a sterile incubator at 37 °C for 4 h.
Wrap samples in sterile gauze and place them in microcentrifuge tubes.
Place prepared samples in the microCT system and scan at 45 keVp, 177 µA, 10.5 µm voxel size, and 300 ms integration.
Export data from the microCT as DICOM files and visualize using software (e.g., OsiriX).
Fix samples for 24 h in a 4% paraformaldehyde solution at the 7-day time point.
Fix fixed samples in a 5% PMA solution for 3 days at the 7-day time point.
Scan samples using the same settings as used in step 8.4.
Segment DICOM files of the IVDs using software with manual thresholding.
Convert the NP and AF volumes into voxel-based finite element meshes using Meshlab.
Combine the microstructures of the NP and AF to form a complete IVD.
Apply experimentally determined boundary conditions in the finite element software.
